sentence_of_record: TEMP-0 (2026-09-14, 598 calls): the 5.7% floor is NOT an unset default: disagreement 0.050 at temperature 0 against 0.057 at the default (-0.007, CI [-0.030, +0.017]); the parameter changes the PROSE (byte-identical responses 0.000 -> 0.177) but not the DECISION; agreement with the default verdicts 0.940, win rate 0.779 under both (8:8, p = 1.00), a quieter judge in style, not a different one, so nothing already measured is invalidated; prediction wrong (0.00-0.03), and the n = 10 amended gate was noise. The +-3pp reading rule is a measured constraint on LLM-judge experiments; the sub-3pp rubric nulls were fought inside a floor no configuration would have removed. Closes J7.

plain_description.what: Re-judges 299 identical matches twice at temperature 0, meaning no sampling randomness (598 calls). It then checks whether the judge's 5.7% disagreement with itself goes away.
plain_description.why: No judge call had ever set a temperature, so the judge's self-disagreement might have been a setting nobody chose, not a property of LLM judging.
plain_description.information: If disagreement vanished, earlier noisy results would need re-reading and a cheap fix would exist. Result: done. Disagreement stayed about the same (5.0% vs 5.7%). Temperature changes the wording of the judge's reply, not its decision. So the roughly 5% noise floor is real, and nothing measured earlier is invalidated. Differences under about 3 points cannot be read reliably. This belongs to the older question pool.
